title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Negation There Is No Mutual Support

questions.question: In the passage, what happens among people who say something is true?
questions.answer: Their statements point to one shared result, so they support one another.

questions.question: What is different about people who deny something?
questions.answer: Each one speaks from his own personal view, so their denials stay separate.

questions.question: Why do many denials not become stronger just because there are many of them?
questions.answer: Because they are not united in one clear proof; they are divided by each person’s own opinion.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the large number of unbelievers who argue against faith?
questions.answer: Their large number does not make their position important or strong against belief.

questions.question: What should be protected in a believer?
questions.answer: A believer’s sure faith and confidence should be protected from doubt.

questions.question: According to the passage, whose ideas caused doubts for some people in this age?
questions.answer: Some philosophers from Europe caused confusion for certain misled people.

questions.question: What happened to those misled people when doubt entered their hearts?
questions.answer: Their certainty was broken, and they lost the happiness that would have lasted forever.

questions.question: How is death described for a person who denies faith?
questions.answer: It is shown as total ending instead of a leaving from this world.

questions.question: How does the grave affect the denier in the passage?
questions.answer: It fills him with fear of being wiped out and makes life bitter.

questions.question: What does the passage say faith really is for a person?
questions.answer: Faith is a huge blessing and the core of real life.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: True belief is strong and life-giving, while denial brings weakness, doubt, and sorrow.

questions.question: In this passage, which is united into one result: affirmation or negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation is united into one result.

questions.question: Why is negation described as many instead of one?
questions.answer: Because each person denies based on his own separate way of seeing things.

questions.question: What phrases show that deniers are speaking from themselves rather than from certainty?
questions.answer: They speak as if saying it is only their own view or belief.

questions.question: If many people reject belief, does that prove they are right?
questions.answer: No. Their number does not prove truth.

questions.question: What harmful effect did certain thinkers have on some people?
questions.answer: They planted doubts that weakened faith.

questions.question: How are the people influenced by those doubts described?
questions.answer: They are described as unfortunate people who were misled.

questions.question: In the passage, what meaning should death have for a believer?
questions.answer: It should be understood as leaving this world, not as complete destruction.

questions.question: How is death wrongly presented by deniers?
questions.answer: They see it as endless non-existence.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of the grave for someone without faith?
questions.answer: It appears like an open doorway to destruction and sadness.

questions.question: What feeling fills the life of a denier because of this view?
questions.answer: Deep sorrow fills his life.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between one affirmation and another affirmation?
questions.answer: They back each other up.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between one denial and another denial?
questions.answer: They do not truly strengthen each other.

questions.question: Why can denials not easily join together into one strong case?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a separate personal judgment.

questions.question: According to the passage, should a believer feel shaken just because deniers seem more numerous?
questions.answer: No. Their apparent majority should not shake a believer.

questions.question: What is especially important not to disturb in a believer?
questions.answer: His settled faith and certainty.

questions.question: What group is blamed for spreading doubt in this age?
questions.answer: Some European philosophers are blamed.

questions.question: What was lost by people who followed those doubts?
questions.answer: They lost firm faith and their everlasting joy.

questions.question: About how many people does the passage say face death every day?
questions.answer: It says thirty thousand people.

questions.question: How do deniers interpret the arrival of death?
questions.answer: They take it as the end of a person forever.

questions.question: Why does the grave become frightening for the denier?
questions.answer: Because he thinks it leads only to annihilation.

questions.question: What effect does that belief have on everyday life?
questions.answer: It makes life painful and full of bitterness.

questions.question: If faith is called the essence of life, what does that suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that life has its deepest value and hope through faith.

questions.question: What is the basic contrast at the start of the passage between affirmation and negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation is single and united, but negation is scattered and many-sided.

questions.question: How does personal opinion affect denial?
questions.answer: It makes each denial separate because it depends on the individual person.

questions.question: Why does the passage say separate denials cannot all hold each other up?
questions.answer: Because they do not rest on one common, positive truth.

questions.question: What should Muslims understand about the apparent strength of unbelievers?
questions.answer: Their seeming strength in numbers has no real weight against truth.

questions.question: What duty is mentioned regarding a believer’s faith?
questions.answer: People should avoid causing doubts in it.

questions.question: In this age, what has harmed some people’s iman according to the passage?
questions.answer: Doubts coming from certain philosophers have harmed it.

questions.question: What kind of people accepted those doubts?
questions.answer: Misled and unfortunate people accepted them.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened to their certainty?
questions.answer: It was ruined.

questions.question: What true meaning of death is taken away by denial?
questions.answer: Death is no longer seen as a departure from this world.

questions.question: What false meaning is put in its place?
questions.answer: It is treated as never existing again.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the grave’s effect on a denier?
questions.answer: It hangs over him as a constant threat and makes his life miserable.

questions.question: When people affirm truth, do their statements lead to one outcome or many outcomes?
questions.answer: They lead to one outcome.

questions.question: When people deny truth, why do many outcomes appear?
questions.answer: Because each person bases denial on his own viewpoint.

questions.question: What does this teach about counting how many people reject belief?
questions.answer: Numbers alone do not decide what is true.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the seeming majority of deniers?
questions.answer: It says their majority does not matter in proving truth.

questions.question: What should not be weakened by spreading hesitation?
questions.answer: A believer’s firm iman should not be weakened.

questions.question: Who is said to have brought such hesitation in this time?
questions.answer: Certain European philosophers are said to have done that.

questions.question: What was the result for those who were fooled by them?
questions.answer: Their sure faith was damaged, and they lost everlasting happiness.

questions.question: What wrong idea about death troubles deniers?
questions.answer: They think death means being completely erased.

questions.question: What symbol in the passage keeps warning the denier of that fearful idea?
questions.answer: The grave does.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from this way of thinking?
questions.answer: It brings intense sadness and poisons life.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the last line of the passage?
questions.answer: Faith is a tremendous blessing and the heart of truly living.

questions.question: In the passage, what kind of statements strengthen one another: positive statements or negative statements?
questions.answer: Positive statements strengthen one another.

questions.question: Why are negative statements not treated the same way?
questions.answer: Because they come from separate personal claims instead of one united truth.

questions.question: If each denier says something based on his own view, what happens to their overall case?
questions.answer: It stays divided and weak.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage make about many unbelievers standing against belief?
questions.answer: Their large number still does not give their denial real importance.

questions.question: What must be guarded carefully in a believer?
questions.answer: His certainty in faith must be guarded.

questions.question: What outside influence is said to have caused doubts in some people?
questions.answer: Ideas of some European philosophers caused those doubts.

questions.question: How are the people who accepted those doubts described in a moral and emotional way?
questions.answer: They are described as pitiable and misled.

questions.question: What two losses came to them through those doubts?
questions.answer: They lost certainty in faith and lost eternal happiness.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the true meaning of death with the false meaning given by deniers?
questions.answer: Truly, death is a departure from this world; falsely, deniers call it total extinction.

questions.question: What does the ever-open grave represent for the denier?
questions.answer: It represents a constant fear of being destroyed forever.

questions.question: How does that fear affect the denier’s life?
questions.answer: It makes life bitter and full of grief.
